{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=distinctions+between+hypothesis-falsification+loops+and+foundational+meta-reasoning+in+autonomous+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"title\": [\"An Engineering Framework for Self-Correcting Autonomous AI Agents: Mitigating Hallucinations and Reasoning Loops in Autonomous Engineering Workflows\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper presents TRACE (Trajectory Reliability and Correction Engine), a runtime self-correction framework for autonomous AI agents in engineering workflows. TRACE targets a reliability gap in multi-step tool-using agents, where unsupported claims, contradictions, repetitive loops, and tool-use anomalies can propagate across long execution trajectories. Existing self-correction methods typically rely on post-hoc reflection or a single intervention mechanism, but do not integrate continuous runtime monitoring, failure attribution, and adaptive recovery in one control layer. TRACE wraps a standard ReAct-style agent with four modules: a Trajectory Monitor, a Failure Attribution module, a Recovery Controller, and an Audit Layer for structured trace logging. We evaluate TRACE on a simulated enterprise incident-triage benchmark of 50 tasks with injected hallucination- and loop-inducing conditions across four difficulty levels. TRACE achieves 76.0% task success versus 68.0% for a self-reflection baseline and 62.0% for vanilla ReAct, while reducing hallucination incidence from 19.4% to 9.6% and loop frequency from 12.1% to 4.8%. The framework is intended for reliable, auditable autonomous execution in engineering environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6956178\", \"title\": [\"Cognitive Internet Layer (CIL): The Foundational Trust and Reasoning Infrastructure for Autonomous Intelligence Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The current internet architecture was fundamentally designed for deterministic data packet transport and applicationlevel request-response interactions, not for the semantic exchange, verification, governance, and replay of autonomous machine reasoning. As autonomous AI agents scale globally to orchestrate critical infrastructure, medical networks, corporate supply chains, and legal workflows, traditional integration patterns create structural bottlenecks. These limitations introduce severe risks of cognitive fragmentation, black-box opacity, and cascade errors across organizational boundaries. This paper proposes the Cognitive Internet Layer (CIL), a protocol-oriented overlay architecture positioned above conventional network transport and below autonomous AI applications. CIL introduces the Reasoning Exchange Protocol (REP) to route structured decision envelopes containing reasoning metadata rather than raw payloads. To resolve real-world deployment trade-offs, the framework integrates Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) for privacy-preserving verification and a Tiered Execution Architecture to isolate highthroughput edge transactions from deep asynchronous multi-agent consensus validation.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6956178\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1080/13546783.2011.553466\", \"title\": [\"From falsification to generating an alternative hypothesis: Exploring the role of the new-perspective hypothesis in successful 2-4-6 task performance\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1080/13546783.2011.553466\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2011, 3, 14]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.65525/svup.9788199565418.2026.117-126\", \"title\": [\"\\\"Meta-Reasoning Agents: Self-Aware Systems for  Autonomous Decision-Making\\\"\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.65525/svup.9788199565418.2026.117-126\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "50230e27d737364f24b3c5b3f55286d7c6c839bc0079e3aaabd8c591226ff667", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6759126", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6956178", "doi:10.1080/13546783.2011.553466", "doi:10.65525/svup.9788199565418.2026.117-126"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6759126", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6956178", "https://doi.org/10.1080/13546783.2011.553466", "https://doi.org/10.65525/svup.9788199565418.2026.117-126"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
